To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the photon strength function for electric dipole transitions in the stable even Mo isotope has been measured in the excitation energy range 4-8.5 MeV and the data were compared with those of other even Mo isotopes and with the results of a novel parametric model.

the electric dipole photon strength function has been determined experimentally over a wide energy range up to the neutron threshold in even Mo nuclei and the results show a strong shape deformation dependence of the E{sub 1} strength.

the photon strength function in nuclei can be derived from photon scattering data in a reliable way and that the electric dipole response in the stable Mo isotopes shows a strong deformation dependence.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel approach for a precise determination of photon strength functions in the energy range of the giant dipole resonance.
the experimental determination of photon strength functions for nuclei of astrophysical and nuclear technology interest.
the study of the electric-dipole strength function of nuclei in the mass range A=92-96.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the E1 strength function of the even Mo isotopic chain has been determined with unprecedented precision and that the data are in good agreement with the predictions of the statistical model.
the electric dipole photon strength function in the even Mo nuclides is not only a function of excitation energy but also depends on the deformation of the nucleus.
the E1 strength function in the stable even Mo nuclei has been determined over a large energy range from 2 MeV up to 8 MeV.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the experimental data obtained by two independent methods and the theoretical analysis of the E1 photon strength function in the Mo isotopes provide new insights into the role of quadrupole shape and triaxial deformation on the electric dipole response.

the electric dipole photon strength in the even molybdenum isotopes was determined over a wide energy range up to the maximum energy of the isov vector giant resonance and that it shows a pronounced deformation dependence.
the electric dipole photon strength function in the even Mo isotope nuclei was measured with two independent techniques and that the results are in excellent agreement.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can use the photon strength function to determine the electric dipole response of a nucleus.
the E1 strength function in the even Mo isotope chain shows a pronounced dependence on the deformation of the nucleus.
the electric dipole photon strength function in the even Mo isotope nuclei is a smooth, quasicontinuum function that can be described by a parametric formula with two free parameters.
